formation.title: The Rise of Austria
formation.text:
The disparate Alpine duchies have been forged into a single realm under our rule. From Vienna, we survey lands stretching from the Danube to the mountain passes, a domain built as much by marriage contracts as by martial prowess. The question now is what kind of state Austria shall become.

Shall we follow the path of the Habsburgs, patient accumulators of crowns through dynastic union, matchmakers who reshape the map of Europe from the bedchamber and the negotiating table? Or shall we embrace our role as Christendom's shield, pouring our strength into the military frontier that guards Europe's eastern flank against all who would threaten it?

This choice unlocks a destiny path in the Traditions tab.

options.text: Let others wage war: we shall marry.

modifiers.name: AEIOU: The Habsburg Way
modifiers.text: Alles Erdreich Ist Oesterreich Untertan. Through strategic marriages, careful alliances, and dynastic accumulation, the House of Habsburg builds its empire not by the sword alone, but through the altar and the treaty table.

options.text: We are the shield of Christendom.

modifiers.name: Antemurale Christianitatis
modifiers.text: Austria stands as the bulwark of Christendom, its armies hardened by generations of frontier warfare against Ottoman expansion. The military frontier stretches from the Adriatic to the Carpathians, defended by a professional soldiery forged in the crucible of perpetual border conflict.

advances.name: Privilegium Maius
advances.text: The forged privileges of Rudolf IV elevate Austria's status among the Imperial territories, granting the Archduchy exceptional legal standing and ceremonial precedence.

advances.name: Kammergut
advances.text: The salt of Hallstatt and Aussee is chamber property: it belongs to the prince and to no one else. Queen Elisabeth set the Hallstatt works in order in 1311 and gave the town its pan house, and in time a salt official at Gmunden came to govern the whole district, its miners, its boatmen and its forests, for the sole purpose of filling the ducal pans.

advances.name: Hofkammer Fiscal Administration
advances.text: Ferdinand I's establishment of the Hofkammer in 1527 centralized Habsburg financial oversight, controlling coinage, mining revenues, tolls, and direct taxation through a permanent bureaucratic institution.

advances.name: Schwaz Silver and Idria Mercury
advances.text: The great mines of Schwaz in Tyrol, once the largest silver mine in Europe, and the mercury deposits at Idria provide the Habsburgs with revenues that underwrite both armies and diplomacy. Below the mines stand the smelting works, where the silver is parted from the copper ore.

advances.name: Landsknechte Tradition
advances.text: Maximilian I's Landsknechte, professional pike-and-shot infantry modeled on the Swiss, form the backbone of Habsburg military power. Their Doppelsöldner front ranks and emphasis on firearms over crossbows mark a revolutionary approach to warfare.

event.title: The Landsknechte of Maximilian
event.text:
Following the devastating Swiss victories at Morat and Nancy, Emperor Maximilian I has commissioned a new type of soldier. Modeled on the fearsome Swiss Reisläufer but loyal to the Habsburg crown, the Landsknechte are professional pike-and-shot infantry organized into Fähnlein of several hundred men. Their front ranks are formed by the Doppelsöldner, experienced soldiers armed with massive Zweihänder swords or arquebuses who earn double pay for standing in the deadliest position.

Maximilian has abolished the crossbow in military use, replacing it entirely with firearms, a bold innovation that puts the Habsburg military at the forefront of the gunpowder revolution. These Landsknechte will become the backbone of Imperial armies across Europe.

options.text: The Emperor's own soldiers stand ready.

advances.name: Festungsbaukunst
advances.text: Habsburg military engineers develop sophisticated fortification systems adapted for the mountainous frontier, incorporating Italian trace italienne principles into Alpine defensive architecture.

advances.name: Militärgrenze
advances.text: The Military Frontier, the Militärgrenze, settles Croatian and Serbian colonists along the Ottoman border, granting them land in exchange for perpetual military service as Grenzer militia.

advances.name: Baroque Court Patronage
advances.text: The Counter-Reformation court at Vienna becomes a center of Baroque splendor. Fischer von Erlach, Hildebrandt, and their successors transform the capital with churches, palaces, and libraries that project Habsburg power and Catholic devotion.

advances.name: Theresian Military Academy
advances.text: Maria Theresa's military academy at Wiener Neustadt, the Theresianum, professionalizes the Habsburg officer corps, training a new generation of commanders in tactics, fortification, and leadership.

advances.name: Imperial Kürassiere
advances.text: The heavy cuirassier regiments of the Habsburg army, armored horsemen charging with pistol and saber, remain a devastating shock force on European battlefields well into the age of gunpowder.

advances.name: Cameralist Institutionalization
advances.text: Cameralism, the systematic science of state management, is institutionalized in Habsburg universities, training bureaucrats in fiscal policy, mining administration, and economic governance.

event.title: The Cameralist State
event.text:
The science of Cameralism (the systematic study of state administration, fiscal policy, and economic management) has taken root in the universities of the Habsburg lands. Where once revenue collection was haphazard and provincial, a new generation of trained bureaucrats now applies rational principles to governance. The Cameralist chairs established in Vienna and Prague produce administrators who understand mining revenues, trade policy, and population management as interconnected systems.

This transformation of the Austrian state from feudal patrimony to rationalized administrative machine will define our capacity to compete with the great powers of Europe.

modifiers.name: Cameralist Administration
modifiers.text: A generation of university-trained Cameralist bureaucrats now manages the state's finances, industries, and population with systematic rationality.

advances.name: Pragmatic Sanction
advances.text: The Pragmatic Sanction of 1713 establishes the legal foundation for indivisible succession of the Habsburg domains, binding the diverse kingdoms and duchies under a single sovereign regardless of the ruler's sex.

event.title: The Pragmatic Sanction
event.text:
Emperor Charles VI, lacking a male heir, has labored for years to secure recognition that the Habsburg domains may pass undivided to a female successor. The Pragmatic Sanction of 1713 establishes the principle of indivisible succession, but its true test will come when the young Maria Theresa inherits the throne and half of Europe moves to dismember her inheritance.

The crisis ahead will demand a choice. Do we invest in the legal and diplomatic framework that binds our diverse domains together through dynastic right? Or do we take Maria Theresa's path, rebuilding the army from its foundations, establishing military academies, and forging a modern fighting force that no coalition can overcome?

options.text: The succession must be secured by law.

modifiers.name: Pragmatic Succession
modifiers.text: The Pragmatic Sanction binds the Habsburg domains in law. Through diplomatic recognition and dynastic right, the indivisibility of our realm is guaranteed.

options.text: The succession must be secured by force.

modifiers.name: Theresian Military Reform
modifiers.text: Following the shock of Silesia's loss, Maria Theresa has overhauled the Habsburg military. Professional training, standardized equipment, and a reformed officer corps transform the imperial army into a modern fighting force.

destiny.name: Habsburg Destiny
destiny.text: Austria has risen from a collection of Alpine duchies to a great power. The realm must now be stabilized before the dynasty can pursue its ultimate ambition, whether through the altar or the sword.

event.title: The Habsburg Destiny
event.text: The formation of Austria marks not an ending but a beginning. From Vienna, the House of Habsburg surveys a realm that stretches across the Alpine heartland, but the dynasty's true destiny lies beyond these mountains. Whether through careful marriages and diplomatic accumulation or through the sword that guards Christendom's eastern gate, Austria's course is set.

destiny.name: The Bohemian Crown
destiny.text: Secure the Crown of Bohemia, the richest kingdom of the Empire, through dynastic claim and diplomacy. Hold Prague and raise it to 45 development, as Rudolf II made it the seat of his court and of the empire.

conditions.text: We own Prague and its development is at least 45

event.title: The Crown of St. Wenceslas
event.text:
The ancient Crown of Bohemia has passed into Habsburg hands. Prague (seat of the Holy Roman Emperor, center of learning and commerce, gateway to the silver mines of Kutna Hora) now answers to Vienna. This is no mere territorial addition but a dynastic revolution. The Bohemian Crown brings with it electoral dignity, vast mineral wealth, and a kingdom whose administrative sophistication rivals any in Europe.

With Bohemia secured, the dynasty's web of marriages and claims can extend further still, westward to the Burgundian inheritance, southward to the Italian crowns.

options.text: Prague and Vienna, united under one crown.

destiny.name: The Burgundian Inheritance
destiny.text: Claim the Burgundian lands in the Low Countries, bringing the wealthy trading cities of Flanders under Habsburg rule. Ghent must be held, and Antwerp held and raised to 49 development: its great markets will finance the dynasty's universal ambitions.

conditions.text: We own Antwerp and its development is at least 49

event.title: The Burgundian Inheritance
event.text:
The great gamble of Habsburg marriage diplomacy has borne its richest fruit. Through the union with the House of Burgundy, the wealthy cities of the Low Countries (Antwerp, Bruges, Ghent) have fallen into Habsburg hands. These are the most commercially sophisticated cities in Europe, their markets handling more trade than entire kingdoms.

This windfall demands a choice. Do we invest in the diplomatic and institutional apparatus needed to govern such far-flung domains, training a generation of Habsburg administrators and negotiators? Or do we exploit the commercial wealth directly, channeling Flemish trade profits into the treasury and building Austria into a mercantile power?

options.text: Train the diplomats who will govern an empire.

modifiers.name: Habsburg Diplomatenakademie
modifiers.text: A generation of Habsburg-trained diplomats and administrators spreads across Europe, skilled in the arts of negotiation, treaty-drafting, and institutional governance that hold the far-flung monarchy together.

options.text: Channel the wealth of Flanders into our coffers.

modifiers.name: Habsburg Handelspolitik
modifiers.text: The commercial wealth of the Low Countries flows through Habsburg channels, enriching the treasury and transforming Austria from a landlocked Alpine state into a mercantile power with interests spanning the continent.

destiny.name: Universalis Monarchia
destiny.text: The Habsburg dream made real, a universal monarchy spanning from the Low Countries to the Italian duchies, bound together by dynastic right and diplomatic mastery. Milan must be held, the treasury full and the house's prestige beyond question.

event.title: Universalis Monarchia
event.text:
The Habsburg dream approaches its apex. From Brussels to Prague, from Vienna to Milan, the dynasty's possessions girdle Europe. No single family has ever held such an expanse of territory through such diverse means, marriage, inheritance, election, and treaty. The question now is how to govern this extraordinary assemblage of peoples, languages, and faiths.

Shall we embrace the principle of cuius regio, eius religio, imposing confessional order while granting enough autonomy to keep the diverse peoples of the monarchy at peace? Or shall we pursue the path of congress diplomacy, making Vienna the capital of European order through negotiation and integration?

modifiers.name: Cuius Regio, Eius Religio
modifiers.text: The principle of confessional coexistence maintains order across the Habsburg domains. Religious tolerance, combined with firm administrative control, allows the monarchy to govern its diverse peoples without fracture.

modifiers.name: Kongressdiplomatie
modifiers.text: Vienna has become the diplomatic capital of Europe. Through congresses, treaties, and patient negotiation, the Habsburgs maintain order across their vast dominions and shape the continent's balance of power.

destiny.name: The Hungarian Campaign
destiny.text: Buda, the ancient seat of the Hungarian kings, must be brought under Habsburg control to anchor the eastern frontier. Raise a powerful army and secure the realm before striking east.

event.title: The Fall of Buda
event.text:
Habsburg armies have entered Buda, the ancient capital of the Hungarian kingdom. For generations this fortress city on the Danube served as the seat of the Arpad and Angevin kings before falling to Ottoman conquest. Now it flies the Habsburg banner once more.

The reconquest of Hungary transforms the strategic map. Austria is no longer a frontier state cowering behind the Leitha. It is the dominant power of the middle Danube, with the military capacity to project force deep into the Balkans.

options.text: Hungary is liberated. The frontier advances.

destiny.name: The Great Turkish War
destiny.text: Push the frontier south into the Ottoman Balkans. Belgrade, the key to the Danube, must fall before Austria can claim mastery of southeastern Europe. An army of 50,000 is required.

event.title: The Great Turkish War
event.text:
Belgrade has fallen. The 'White Fortress' (key to the Danube, gateway to the Ottoman Balkans) is in Habsburg hands. Prince Eugene's campaigns have shattered Ottoman power in Hungary and pushed the frontier deep into Serbia. This is the greatest victory Christendom has won against the Ottomans since Lepanto.

The question now is how to consolidate these vast conquests. Do we invest in logistics and supply infrastructure, building the road networks and depots that will sustain future campaigns and allow the devastated borderlands to recover? Or do we perfect the art of siege warfare that won Belgrade, ensuring our engineers and artillerists remain the finest in Europe?

options.text: Build the roads that sustain an empire.

modifiers.name: Kaiserliche Versorgungslinien
modifiers.text: A network of military roads, supply depots, and river transport routes sustains Habsburg armies across the vast Danubian theater, enabling rapid reinforcement and recovery of war-ravaged borderlands.

options.text: Perfect the science of fortress warfare.

modifiers.name: Belagerungskunst
modifiers.text: Habsburg military engineers have perfected the art of scientific siege warfare. Their artillery batteries and approach to fortress reduction are the finest in Europe, though maintaining such expertise strains the treasury.

destiny.name: Bollwerk des Glaubens
destiny.text: Austria stands as the unshakeable bulwark of Christendom, its Military Frontier stretching from the Adriatic to the Carpathians. Zagreb must be held, and Karlovac, the star fortress Archduke Charles raised from nothing in 1579 as the seat of the Croatian frontier, held and raised to 28 development.

conditions.text: We own Karlovac and its development is at least 28

event.title: Bollwerk des Glaubens
event.text:
Austria stands as the undisputed shield of Christendom. The Military Frontier stretches unbroken from the Adriatic to the Carpathians, manned by generations of Grenzer settlers who know no life but war. Behind this living wall, the Habsburg domains have grown into a great power whose armies have broken every threat from the east.

This achievement demands a final choice. Do we embrace the crusading spirit that drove us here, sanctifying our wars, cheapening our casus belli against the infidel, and steeling our people for perpetual struggle? Or do we turn inward, imposing imperial order on the conquered lands, building schools and courts that will civilize the frontier and make it truly ours?

modifiers.name: Kreuzzugsgeist
modifiers.text: The spirit of crusade burns in the Habsburg state. Wars against those of different faith come cheaply, morale remains high through extended campaigns, and the cause of Christendom provides endless justification for further conquests.

options.text: The frontier must be governed, not merely held.

modifiers.name: Kaiserliche Ordnung
modifiers.text: Imperial order replaces martial law on the conquered frontier. Schools, courts, and administrative offices transform wild borderlands into productive provinces, though the shift from raiding to governing reduces the spoils of war.

units.name: Imperial Kürassiere
units.text: Heavy armored cavalry of the Habsburg army, charging into enemy lines with devastating shock force. Equipped with half-armor, pistols, and heavy sabers.

units.name: Grenzer Militia
units.text: Croatian and Serbian frontier settlers who serve as light infantry on the Military Frontier, defending the Habsburg border against Ottoman raids in exchange for land grants.

buildings.name: Hofkammer
buildings.text: The Court Chamber, central fiscal administration office of the Habsburg state, overseeing mining revenues, coinage, tolls, and tax collection through a permanent bureaucratic staff.

buildings.name: Schmelzhütte
buildings.text: A smelting works in the valley below the mine, like the one recorded at Brixlegg from 1463. The ore of Schwaz holds copper and silver together, and here they are parted.

children.text: The location's raw material is Silver
The location's raw material is Copper

buildings.name: Pfannhaus
buildings.text: A ducal pan house. Brine led down from the salt mountain in wooden pipes is boiled dry in a great iron pan, and the salt is packed in conical moulds for the boats that carry it down the Traun.

where.text: The location's raw material is Salt

buildings.name: Habsburg Festung
buildings.text: A star-fort fortification built according to Habsburg engineering principles, combining Italian trace italienne design with adaptations for the mountainous Alpine frontier.

buildings.name: Cameralist Institut
buildings.text: A center of Cameralist education and research, training bureaucrats in the systematic science of state management, fiscal policy, mining administration, trade regulation, and population governance.

buildings.name: Theresianum
buildings.text: A military academy in the tradition of Maria Theresa's reforms at Wiener Neustadt, training officers in modern tactics, siege engineering, and military leadership.

buildings.name: Hofburg Chancellery
buildings.text: The great palace-chancellery of the Habsburg universal monarchy, housing the diplomatic corps, state archives, and administrative apparatus that governs domains spanning half of Europe.

buildings.name: Grenzfestung
buildings.text: A major fortress complex of the Military Frontier, anchoring the Habsburg defensive line with heavy fortifications, permanent garrison, and stockpiled armaments against any eastern incursion.

list.name: Generalquartiermeisterstab
list.text: The quartermaster general's staff, created in the Seven Years' War after the defeat at Leuthen in 1757, with Franz Moritz von Lacy as chief of staff to Field Marshal Daun. Its officers chose the camps, laid out the marches and kept the maps, and after the war they surveyed the monarchy sheet by sheet. A campaign was no longer improvised by its commander: a trained staff planned it for him, and the generals of the next generation were schooled in its rooms.

list.name: Geheime Konferenz
list.text: The Privy Conference, evolved from Ferdinand I's Geheimer Rat and given its classical form by Leopold I after 1665, when the old council had grown too large to keep a secret. A small inner council of five to seven hand-picked grandees (Auersperg, Lobkowitz, Schwarzenberg, later Kaunitz) deliberated on dynastic marriages, war and peace, and the Spanish succession. Its protocols, preserved in the Haus-, Hof- und Staatsarchiv, became the chief register of Habsburg high diplomacy and the school in which generations of imperial statesmen were trained.

list.name: Hungarian Cancellaria
list.text: The Magyar Udvari Kancellaria, the separate Hungarian Court Chancery established at Pozsony and confirmed by the Diet of 1606. The Hungarian nobility refused to be administered through the German-language Hofkanzlei in Vienna; the Cancellaria preserved the constitutional doctrine that Hungary was a regnum independens, united with Austria only in the person of the king. The crown bought stability with the Magyar magnates at the price of permanent dual administration.

list.name: Tiroler Landlibell
list.text: The defence ordinance that Maximilian I gave the county of Tyrol on 23 June 1511. The estates of the land, its peasants and towns among them, were bound to field from 5,000 to 20,000 men according to the danger, and every able man could be called out behind them. In return they served only inside Tyrol, and no war that touched the land was to be begun without their consent. The valleys kept their own companies of marksmen under it for centuries.

list.name: Directorium in Publicis et Cameralibus
list.text: The central administrative body imposed by Friedrich Wilhelm Graf von Haugwitz on 2 May 1749 after the loss of Silesia exposed the bankruptcy of estate-based finance. The Directorium subordinated the Bohemian and Austrian Hofkanzleien and the Hofkammer into a single college, centralizing tax assessment, recruit-quota allocation and the Theresian cadaster. The provincial Landstände lost their constitutional veto over the Contributionale; permanent salaried Kreishauptleute replaced noble tax-collectors in the countryside.

list.name: Josephinismus
list.text: The Josephinist reform programme of 1780 to 1790, centered on the Toleranzpatent of 13 October 1781 (recognizing Lutheran, Calvinist and Greek-Orthodox confession) together with the Edict of Tolerance for the Jews of 1782, the abolition of personal serfdom in 1781, and the dissolution of contemplative monasteries with their endowments redirected to a Religionsfond funding parish priests and primary schools. Joseph II ruled by decree through the Hofstellen, displacing the prelacy and the estate diets in favor of cameralist Beamte trained at the Theresianum.
